input.title: Add lang="en" to the <html> element
input.rationale: The <html> element has no lang attribute, so screen readers can't tell which language to read the page in. The title, logo alt text, search label and body copy are all in English. "Handmade pottery for everyday use…" and "our studio in Leeds" are examples. This patch sets lang="en". The studio is in Leeds, so "en-GB" would also be correct if you want to name the regional variant. That's your call. The patch is limited to the lang attribute on the element at offset 16. It doesn't confirm the page meets any wider accessibility standard.
